purpose: Convert the accumulated 1942-44 search/radar/ESM/RI-DF/COMINT and HAILSTONE lessons into a theater-level Pacific ISR maturity model. The system is mature for warning, sector narrowing and dispersal, not for automatic long-range weapon-quality carrier fixes.

traffic_analysis_RI_DF_and_COMINT.effect: Can recognize unusual US fast-carrier traffic/logistics patterns and narrow likely operational sectors. Cannot routinely read highest-grade US operational content or identify exact carrier coordinates.

fixed_base_warning_plot_priority_nodes.effect: Palau-class priority nodes can combine radar, visual posts, DF, weather, plot, fighter readiness and AA alert into a useful local warning/defense loop.

wide_area_maritime_search.effect: Flying boats, seaplanes, land reconnaissance and selected submarines/pickets can cover likely approach sectors efficiently when cued; still constrained by weather, aircraft availability, navigation and enemy CAP.

recontact_and_track_maintenance.effect: Suspicious contacts are revisited and multiple reports are correlated. Long-range fast-carrier tracks still expire often because the target moves quickly and reconnaissance aircraft are vulnerable.

long_range_weapon_quality_cueing.effect: Insufficient by itself for a coordinated Japanese carrier strike. Normally requires a recent visual/submarine contact plus predicted movement and favorable weather/communications.

command_acceptance_and_alert_persistence.effect: Post-HAILSTONE doctrine no longer treats one negative search as reason to stand down when traffic/DF/visual cues remain convergent. This is a major soft-progress gain.

fleet_CIC_equivalence.effect: Selected ships have better radar/plot/ESM integration, but there is no fleet-wide US-style CIC/centimetric-radar equivalence. Tactical fighter direction and mobile recontact remain uneven.

system_logic: Use traffic/DF/passive cues to narrow the ocean sector.
Send scarce long-range reconnaissance, submarines or pickets into the narrowed sector.
Demand a confirmation/recontact cycle before releasing mobile carriers.
If confirmation is stale but threat probability is high, disperse fixed high-value assets and raise base readiness rather than sortie blindly.
Keep warning and weapon-quality targeting as separate thresholds.
soft_learning_inputs: routine ESM-cued reconnaissance and electronics field-service practice
guardrails: Do not turn one RWR/DF bearing into a carrier position.
Do not grant fleet-wide US CIC performance.
Do not let strategic warning automatically release the four-carrier core.
Do not reset alert to normal merely because one reconnaissance sweep is negative.
strategic_conclusion: By late March 1944 the Branch Japanese system is credible at theater warning and asset preservation. Its weakest remaining link is persistent mobile-ocean tracking to a fresh strike-quality solution.
